Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with acute pain and
swelling of the left wrist. Imaging confirmed a distal radius fracture, and the
physical examination findings were consistent with that diagnosis. The mechanism of
injury, a forward impact transmitted through an outstretched hand, is well matched to
the nature and severity of the fracture. No prior injury or treatment involving this
wrist is known from the history obtained. Care was delivered over 34 visits, beginning
with immobilization and orthopedic follow-up, then progressing to supervised
range-of-motion and strengthening exercises. Treatment followed a typical recovery
course, with visit frequency decreasing as function and pain improved. Billing records
reflect single charges for each service rendered, with no duplicated or repeated
entries. At discharge the patient had improved grip strength and wrist mobility and
was released to independent home exercise.
